longevity.headline: Physical Activity Linked to Slower Ovarian Aging via Adiponectin Pathway
longevity.summary: Based on the paper title and linked discussion (as the published abstract is unavailable), this study combined observational analysis of 152,435 UK Biobank participants with mouse mechanistic models. Researchers found that higher physical activity levels correlated with delayed ovarian aging in humans. In mice, physical activity appeared to preserve ovarian reserve and extend reproductive lifespan by boosting ovarian adiponectin signaling, a protective effect absent in adiponectin-knockout models. While the rodent experiments demonstrate causal pathways for adiponectin, the human findings remain observational and subject to confounding, and animal reproductive timelines differ significantly from human biology. Practical meaning: Regular physical activity supports broad metabolic health, but more research is needed to determine how directly it influences human reproductive longevity.

primaryLinks.title: Physical activity delays ovarian aging in part through adiponectin-related signaling pathways

longevity.headline: Lower Plasma Selenium Linked to Higher All-Cause and Cancer Mortality in Older Adults
longevity.summary: In an observational cohort study of 1,389 older adults followed over 9 years (the EVA study), researchers examined baseline plasma selenium concentrations and mortality. Over the follow-up period, 101 participants died. After adjusting for sociodemographic factors, diet, baseline health, and cognitive status, lower plasma selenium (per 0.2 µmol/L decrement) was associated with an increased risk of all-cause mortality (adjusted RR 1.54, 95% CI 1.25–1.88) and cancer-related mortality (adjusted RR 1.79, 95% CI 1.32–2.44). As an observational analysis, this study demonstrates association rather than causation; lower selenium levels may reflect poor nutritional status, underlying illness, or other unmeasured confounders. Practical meaning: Meeting baseline dietary selenium requirements supports general nutritional health, but observational findings do not indicate that taking selenium supplements will lower mortality risk.

primaryLinks.title: Selenium and mortality in the elderly: results from the EVA study.

longevity.headline: 21-Protein Blood Panel Shows Promise in Distinguishing Dementia Types
longevity.summary: In an observational study analyzing 1,318 plasma samples and an independent validation cohort of 805 individuals, researchers developed a 21-protein multiplex blood panel to differentiate between Alzheimer’s disease, dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB), and frontotemporal dementia (FTD). Distinct protein signatures emerged: glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) increased across the Alzheimer’s continuum, integrins alpha-V and alpha-M were reduced in DLB (including autopsy-confirmed cases), and elevated neurofilament light chain paired with lower GFAP was linked to FTD. A key limitation is that these findings reflect biomarker profiling in curated research cohorts and require prospective clinical trials to establish real-world diagnostic utility. Practical meaning: Multi-protein blood tests may eventually help clinicians tell major dementia subtypes apart without invasive procedures, but the test is not yet available for routine medical care.

primaryLinks.title: Plasma proteome profiling identified biomarkers for the differential diagnosis and molecular staging of neurodegenerative dementias

longevity.headline: Critical review challenges sirtuins as evolutionarily conserved longevity genes
longevity.summary: In a critical review of evolutionary and model-organism biology, the author evaluates whether sirtuin genes (such as SIR2 and its homologs) function as universal regulators of lifespan. The analysis highlights that initial reports of lifespan extension in yeast, worms, and flies were frequently confounded by genetic background artifacts and reporting biases. Furthermore, SIR2 acts as a pro-aging factor in yeast chronological aging and in flies under amino-acid deprivation. The review concludes that evidence does not support sirtuins as conserved lifespan determinants or as the primary mediators of NAD+ metabolism. The main limitation is that this is a conceptual and narrative review reflecting an ongoing scientific dispute rather than a new empirical trial. Practical meaning: Popular claims that sirtuin activation reliably drives lifespan extension remain scientifically contested and unproven in humans.

primaryLinks.title: Sirtuins are not conserved longevity genes
A critical assessment of the information theory of aging

longevity.headline: Midlife Blood Metabolites Linked to Brain Structure and Cognitive Health
longevity.summary: In an observational study of 1,082 dementia-free middle-aged adults from the Rotterdam Study (replicated in two independent older cohorts), researchers analyzed 991 blood metabolites alongside cognitive tests and brain MRI scans. Fourteen metabolites consistently correlated with cognitive performance, with the diet-derived antioxidant ergothioneine showing the strongest association. The metabolite pattern linked to poorer midlife cognition mirrored markers of incident Alzheimer's disease. Modifiable factors like lifestyle and medications accounted for up to 28.6% of metabolite variation; notably, antacid use was linked to lower ergothioneine levels, accounting for roughly 31.5% of the statistical association between antacids and lower cognitive scores. Because this is an observational study, these findings show associations rather than direct causation, and residual confounding remains possible. Practical meaning: While blood markers like ergothioneine provide clues about brain aging pathways, these findings are preliminary and do not justify taking supplements or altering prescribed medications without clinical guidance.

primaryLinks.title: The blood metabolome of brain health in midlife and influences of genes, microbiome and exposome

longevity.headline: 'Metabolically Healthy' Obesity Linked to Higher Long-Term Cardiovascular and Mortality Risks
longevity.summary: In a prospective cohort study of 157,159 UK Biobank participants followed for a median of 12.9 years, researchers examined whether obesity without baseline hypertension, diabetes, or dyslipidemia is truly benign. Compared to normal-weight individuals with no metabolic abnormalities, those with obesity but no metabolic abnormalities had significantly higher risks of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (hazard ratio [HR] 1.46 in men, 1.34 in women), heart failure (HR 1.63 in men, 1.69 in women), liver disease (MASLD; HR 2.37 in men, 4.44 in women), and all-cause mortality (HR 1.36 in men, 1.27 in women). Risks escalated substantially when metabolic abnormalities were also present. Because this is an observational study, it demonstrates association rather than direct causation, and baseline metabolic status may have changed over the follow-up period. Practical meaning: Normal blood pressure, lipids, and glucose do not completely eliminate the elevated long-term cardiovascular and liver risks associated with obesity, supporting discussions with a clinician on comprehensive weight and metabolic health management.

primaryLinks.title: Obesity, metabolic health status, and adverse outcomes in men and women.

longevity.headline: Estrogen Therapy Linked to Lower Alzheimer's Neuropathology in Cohort Study
longevity.summary: Note: Because the full abstract was unavailable at review, this summary is based on the linked study report and public discussion. In an observational analysis across two US cohorts, researchers evaluated post-mortem brain tissue in women to assess whether menopausal estrogen therapy was associated with Alzheimer's disease neuropathology and dementia diagnoses. According to study reports, past estrogen use was associated with approximately 35% lower odds of Alzheimer's pathology at autopsy alongside fewer clinical dementia diagnoses. As an observational study, this demonstrates correlation rather than causation, and findings may be influenced by healthy-user bias or differences in baseline health between hormone users and non-users. Practical meaning: Hormone therapy decisions are complex and individualised; discuss the broader risks and benefits with your doctor rather than starting treatment solely for dementia prevention.

primaryLinks.title: Association Between Menopausal Hormone Therapy and Alzheimer Disease Neuropathology

longevity.headline: Physical Fitness Associated with Lower All-Cause Mortality in Older Adults
longevity.summary: Because full study details and an abstract are unavailable, this summary is based on the linked discussion of a study in JAMA Network Open investigating physical fitness and all-cause mortality among older adults. Observational research in this domain typically evaluates measures of cardiorespiratory or muscular fitness against long-term survival outcomes. While higher fitness levels are consistently associated with lower all-cause mortality, observational designs cannot establish direct causation and are subject to confounding factors, such as baseline health status and reverse causality. Practical meaning: Maintaining baseline physical fitness and regular activity remains a foundational, low-risk habit associated with better long-term survival in older age.

primaryLinks.title: Physical Fitness and All-Cause Mortality in Older Adults

longevity.headline: Plant-Based Fats Linked to Modestly Lower Cardiovascular and All-Cause Mortality
longevity.summary: In a prospective cohort analysis of 407,531 US adults in the NIH-AARP Diet and Health Study followed over 24 years, researchers evaluated the relationship between dietary fat sources and mortality. Comparing the highest to lowest quintile of intake, higher plant fat consumption—particularly from grains and vegetable oils—was associated with a lower risk of all-cause mortality (adjusted absolute risk difference [ARD] -1.10%; HR 0.91) and cardiovascular disease (CVD) mortality (adjusted ARD -0.73%; HR 0.86). Conversely, higher animal fat intake was associated with higher overall mortality (adjusted ARD +0.78%; HR 1.16) and CVD mortality (adjusted ARD +0.32%; HR 1.14). Modeling the replacement of 5% of daily energy from animal fat with plant fat was associated with a 4% to 24% reduction in overall mortality risk. As an observational study relying on self-reported baseline dietary questionnaires, these findings reflect associations rather than proven causation, and residual lifestyle confounding remains possible. Practical meaning: Swapping some dietary animal fats for plant-based sources like vegetable oils and whole grains aligns with broad, low-risk cardiovascular dietary patterns.

primaryLinks.title: Plant and Animal Fat Intake and Overall and Cardiovascular Disease Mortality.

longevity.headline: JAMA Publication Highlights the Role of Sleep Health in Obesity Management
longevity.summary: Based on linked discussion from the study authors, a new article in JAMA addresses how sleep health impacts obesity prevention and treatment. Because the detailed abstract was unavailable at the time of writing, specific study design, population characteristics, and effect sizes cannot be verified from the announcement alone. While established literature demonstrates strong links between sleep disruption and metabolic dysregulation, distinguishing direct causal effects from broader behavioral confounding requires evaluating the full study data. Practical meaning: Consistent, restorative sleep is a recognized component of overall metabolic wellness, though specific clinical weight-management plans should be coordinated with a physician.

primaryLinks.title: JAMA Article on Sleep Health and Obesity

longevity.headline: Study Highlights Causes of US Excess Mortality Compared to Other High-Income Nations
longevity.summary: Based on the linked discussion of a study published in JAMA Network Open (full abstract unavailable), researchers analyzed the primary factors contributing to rising excess deaths in the United States compared to peer high-income nations. The report indicates that this widening mortality disparity is driven largely by increases in circulatory and metabolic diseases, as well as substance- and mental-health-related causes such as drug poisonings, alcohol-related deaths, and suicide. Because full study parameters and effect sizes were unavailable from the discussion, this summary reflects broad epidemiological associations rather than detailed individual-level causal analyses. Practical meaning: Sustaining long-term health requires prioritizing foundational cardiometabolic risk management alongside vigilance around mental health and substance misuse.

primaryLinks.title: Causes of Excess Deaths in the US Compared With Other High-Income Countries
